overview: This file documents U.S. monitoring of the registration and flag status of Japanese-linked vessels in Latin America during 1940–1941. A cross-reference sheet points to a Naval Attaché report concerning the transfer of the S.S. Atlantico from U.S. to Panamanian registry and its reported subsequent transfer to Japanese registry. Two departmental copies of a September 1941 message report that Costa Rica cancelled the registration of the Japanese fishing vessel Amano at Puntarenas, reflecting heightened wartime scrutiny of Japanese maritime activity in the Americas.

people.name: Claude G. Bowers
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Chile and apparent sender of the referenced despatch

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch on transfer of the S.S. Atlantico’s registry
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to despatch no. 871 concerning the transfer of the S.S. Atlantico from U.S. to Panamanian and reportedly Japanese registry.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference records a Naval Attaché report about changes in the registry of the S.S. Atlantico. It states that the vessel was transferred from U.S. to Panamanian registry and reportedly thereafter to Japanese registry. The original document was filed as despatch no. 871 under file number 894.24/1108½.

subfiles.title: Naval Attaché message on cancellation of the Amano’s Costa Rican registration
subfiles.about: The message reports Costa Rica’s cancellation of the registration of the Japanese fishing vessel Amano at Puntarenas.
subfiles.summary: A paraphrased message received from the Naval Attaché in Guatemala states that the Costa Rican government cancelled the registration of the Japanese fishing vessel Amano on September 9, 1941. The vessel had been registered at Puntarenas. The page bears Department of State receipt and later declassification markings.

subfiles.title: Strictly confidential departmental copy of the Amano registration message
subfiles.about: This filing copy repeats the report that Costa Rica cancelled the Amano’s registration at Puntarenas.
subfiles.summary: Page 3 is a file-number and routing cover associated with document 894.851/3. Page 4 contains a strictly confidential paraphrase of the September 9 message from the Naval Attaché in Guatemala, duplicating the report that Costa Rica cancelled the Japanese fishing vessel Amano’s registration at Puntarenas. Numerous Department of State receipt, routing, filing, and declassification stamps show the document’s administrative handling.

interest: The file provides a compact view of how the State Department tracked changes in the nationality and legal status of Japanese-linked shipping in the Western Hemisphere immediately before the United States entered the Second World War. The juxtaposition of the Atlantico flag-transfer reference with the cancellation of the Amano’s Costa Rican registration is useful for studying maritime surveillance, flagging practices, and Latin American restrictions on Japanese activity. The duplicate Amano messages and their routing stamps also reveal the internal circulation, classification, and later declassification of naval intelligence within the Department of State.
